official.description_text:
Postdoc in Hospital Energy Systems and Infrastructure Resilience
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Architecture and Built Environment
Job description
This project investigates energy optimisation and resilience of critical infrastructure, focusing on hospitals. The researcher will model hospital HVAC, heating, cooling and backup energy systems and examine their dependencies on wider energy and healthcare supply chains. Research combines dynamic energy simulation, scenario-based risk and resilience assessment, life-cycle assessment (LCA) and environmental product declaration (EPD) data to quantify energy performance, environmental impacts and service continuity during climate-related disruptions. Building on these analyses, the researcher will develop and assess advanced control and decision-support methods, potentially including AI, to improve efficiency, flexibility and operational resilience. Validation will emphasise realistic operating constraints and collaboration with healthcare and infrastructure stakeholders. The position includes 20% teaching or departmental duties.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
PhD in building energy engineering, energy systems, HVAC, control engineering or a related discipline.
Experience in building energy modelling, simulation and optimisation, including thermal comfort assessment.
Ability to analyse complex technical systems and communicate findings in scientific papers and technical reports.
Strong written and spoken English, as this will be required in day-to-day work.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Knowledge of supply-chain risks, critical-infrastructure resilience and scenario-based assessment.
Experience with LCA, EPDs and environmental impact modelling.
Experience with advanced or AI-based control, hospital technical systems and real-world implementation.
Skills in preparing project deliverables, research proposals and presentations; teaching experience.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral researcher position in building energy systems, focusing on hospital HVAC, heating, cooling, and backup energy systems. Research combines dynamic energy simulation, risk/resilience assessment, lifecycle assessment (LCA), and advanced control methods (potentially AI-based). Includes 20% teaching or departmental duties.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position focuses on building energy engineering, infrastructure resilience, and HVAC systems—domains unrelated to human-computer interaction, immersive systems, spatial cognition, or learning science. While the posting mentions 'healthcare stakeholders' and realistic operating constraints, the core research is technical (energy modelling, simulation, control systems), not human-centred design or user-facing technology.

methodological_fit.rationale: Requires expertise in building energy modelling, dynamic thermal simulation, lifecycle assessment (LCA), and advanced control systems. The researcher has intermediate experimental design and quantitative research skills (from user studies), but no background in building physics, energy simulation tools, LCA methodology, or HVAC systems. The technical focus (energy systems, control algorithms) differs from user-centred evaluation and immersive learning assessment.

growth_value.rationale: Would develop expertise in energy systems, resilience assessment, and potentially AI-based control strategies. These skills do not advance human-centred XR or spatial cognition research. Limited transferable value to the researcher's target identity unless reframed around human factors in hospital operations—which is not the focus.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH (Sweden, preferred country) is reputable. The School of Architecture and Built Environment emphasizes sustainability and real-world impact, which aligns with values. However, supervisor expertise is in building energy systems, not HCI or immersive systems. Postdoctoral position is appropriate career stage, but the research direction diverges from target identity. Limited connection to immersive-systems or spatial-cognition research networks.
